Rashi on Eruvin 104a:10:1.hebrew: בהולכת אברים לכבש דלאו עבודה היא - לעולם לא מבטל ליה, אלא לאחר דריסה מולחין ממנו עורות קדשים. ודקשיא לך: "הא הוי חציצה?" — לא תקשה, דהא דקתני "בוזקין מלח", בהולכת אברים לכבש קאמר, דלאו עבודה; דקא ס"ד השתא, דכיון דכל הכפרה תלויה בדם, אע"ג דהקטר חלבים הוה עבודה, הולכה דידהו מיהא לא חשיב:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:10:1.english: Regarding the bringing of the limbs to the ramp, which is not a service - In fact, he does not nullify it; rather, after [it has been] trodden upon, they salt the hides of sacrificial animals with it. And as for that which was difficult to you — "Does this not constitute an interposition?" — do not find it difficult, for that which was taught, "[one may] scatter salt," it was stated regarding the bringing of the limbs to the ramp, which is not a service; for it enters [the Gemara's] mind now that since all atonement is dependent on the blood, even though the burning of the fats is a service, their transport at least is not considered [such].

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:11:1.hebrew: והקריב את הכל - רישא דקרא: ״והקרב והכרעים ירחץ במים״, אלמא באברים קמשתעי קרא. ומדבעי כהונה — שמע מינה עבודה היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:11:1.english: And he shall offer it whole - The beginning of the verse [states]: “And the innards and the shins he shall wash in water”; evidently, the verse is speaking of the limbs. And since it requires a priest, learn from this that it is a [sacrificial] service.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:12:1.english: And scatters [straw] in it - [In order] to tread upon it.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:12:2.english: Neither with a basket nor with a hamper - In the manner of a weekday.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:12:3.english: The bottom of the basket - [A basket] that broke and the bottom remained.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:14:1.english: Knocked on the door - He struck the door with his fist and produced a sound.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:14:2.english: As he desecrates Shabbat - For he holds that producing any sound is forbidden.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:15:1.english: [Regarding] a musical sound - That is heard like music, melodiously and gently.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:15:2.hebrew: מעלין בדיופי - מעלין יין מחבית לחבית ע"י שני קנים החתוכים באלכסון, ומניח ראשין המשופעים זה כנגד זה, ונותן אחד מן הקנים בחבית, ומוצץ בפיו בראש הקנה האחר מעט מן היין אליו, ומסלק משם, והיין יוצא כולו מאליו. דיופי — שתי פיות:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:15:2.english: One may draw up with a siphon [diyofei] - One transfers wine from [one] barrel to [another] barrel by means of two reeds cut diagonally: he places their slanted ends opposite each other, places one of the reeds into the barrel, sucks with his mouth at the end of the other reed a little of the wine toward himself, and removes [his mouth] from there, and all the wine flows out on its own. Diyofei [means] two mouths.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:15:3.hebrew: ומטיפין מיארק לחולה - כלי הוא, ופיו צר, ושל מתכת הוא, ומנוקב בתחתיתו נקבים נקבים דקין. וממלא מים וסותם פיו העליון, וכל זמן שפיו סתום, אין המים יוצאין בנקבים התחתונים. וכשרוצה, נוטל פקק העליון, והמים יוצאין בנקבים טיף אחר טיף; ונותן כלי מתכת וכופהו תחתיו, וקולן נשמע לחולה:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:15:3.english: And one may drip [water from a] miarak for an ill person - It is a vessel, and its opening is narrow, and it is made of metal, and it is perforated at its bottom with tiny holes. And one fills [it with] water and stops up its upper opening, and as long as its opening is stopped up, the water does not come out through the lower holes. And when he wishes, he removes the upper stopper, and the water emerges through the holes, drop by drop; and he places a metal vessel and overturns it beneath it, and their sound is heard by the ill person.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:16:1.hebrew: וקא בעי לאתעורי - ע"י קול זה, ומתיראין להקיצו בידים שמא יבעית. וכיון דלהקיץ הוא, לא בנעימה ובנחת נשמע, שהרי קול נעים מרדימו והולך — אפ"ה לבריא לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:16:1.english: And they wish to awaken him - By means of this sound, and they are afraid to awaken him by hand lest he be startled. And since it is to awaken [him], it is not heard in a pleasant and soothing manner, for a pleasant sound steadily lulls him to sleep; even so, for a healthy person [it is] not [permitted].

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:17:1.english: Zimzumei - *Cenbes* [Old French for bells or cymbals].

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:18:1.english: Nor slap - [Striking] his hands against his chest.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:18:2.english: He shall clap - [Striking] palm against palm.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:18:3.hebrew: ירקד - ברגל, להשמיע קול להבעית העופות:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:18:3.english: [Nor] dance - With the foot, to make a sound to frighten the birds.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:19:1.hebrew: שמא יטול צרור - ויזרוק לרה"ר להבריח העופות:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:19:1.english: Lest he pick up a pebble - And throw [it] into the public domain to chase away the birds.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:1:1.english: Three by three [fingerbreadths] interpose - And [this is] on account of an excess of garments.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:20:1.hebrew: משחקות באגוזים - לגלגלן דרך דף, ומכות זו את זו, כדרך שמשחקות הנשים:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:20:1.english: [Women] who play with nuts - To roll them along a board, and they strike one another, in the manner that women play.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:21:1.english: To level holes - To prepare a path for rolling the nut.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:22:1.english: With apples - [This is] also in this manner.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:22:2.english: Producing a sound - That the wheel emits a sound.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:24:1.hebrew: גזרה שמא ימלא לגינתו - מתוך שממלאין בו בלא טורח, אתי להשקות בו בגינתו וחורבתו בשבת:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:24:1.english: A decree lest he draw [water] for his garden - Since one draws [water] with it without effort, he will come to irrigate his garden and his ruin with it on Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:2:1.hebrew: לימא פליגא - הא דרבא אדרב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא, דחשיב צלצול קטן יתור בגדים:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:2:1.english: Shall we say [this] disagrees - [Does] this [teaching] of Rava [disagree] with [that of] Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya, who considers a small sash [to be an] excess of garments?

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:2:2.hebrew: שאני צלצול דחשיב - ואיכא למימר דמודה בה רבא, אבל רבי יוחנן פליג עליה, דהא עלה קאי ופליג:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:2:2.english: A sash is different, as it is significant - And one can say that Rava agrees with this, but Rabbi Yoḥanan disputes him, for he was addressing it and disputing [it].

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:3:1.english: And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan - Who said that a sash is also permitted:

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:3:2.hebrew: לישמעינן - תנא דמתניתין צלצול קטן דלא חייץ, וכ"ש גמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:3:2.english: Let [it] teach us - [Let] the Tanna of our Mishnah [teach us about] a small sash, that it does not interpose, and all the more so a reed.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:4:1.hebrew: דגמי מסי - משום שבת איצטריך למתני גמי, דאף על גב דמסי — שרי במקדש:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:4:1.english: That a reed heals - On account of Shabbat it was necessary to teach [the case of] a reed, [namely,] that even though it heals, it is permitted in the Temple.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:5:1.hebrew: בוזקין מלח - מפזרין ומכתתין על הכבש, מפני שחלק הוא, וכשהגשמים נופלין עליו הוא מחליק. בוזקין — לשון כיתות, כדאמר בפרק ב' דיומא (דף כב:): ״ממאי דהאי 'ויפקדם בבזק' מידי דמיבזק הוא?״ ועוד, ״כמראה הבזק״ מפרש בחגיגה (דף יג:): ״כאור היוצא בין החרסים״ — שצורפין בהן זהב, והם נקובים וסדוקים, ולהב היוצא בנקב יש בו כמראה ירקרק או אדמדם:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:5:1.english: One may scatter salt - They scatter and crush [salt] on the ramp, because it is smooth, and when rain falls upon it, it becomes slippery. Bozekin [scattering] is an expression of crushing, as [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Yoma (22b): "From where [do we know] that this [phrase], 'And he numbered them with a bezek' [I Samuel 11:8], [means] something that is crushed?" And furthermore, "like the appearance of the bazak" [Ezekiel 1:14] is explained in Chagigah (13b): "like the light emerging from between the earthenware shards" — in which they refine gold, and they are perforated and cracked, and the flame emerging from the hole has an appearance that is greenish or reddish.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:5:2.hebrew: וממלאין מבור הגדול כו' - כך שמן, ושניהם בלשכת העזרה:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:5:2.english: And one may draw water from the Great Cistern, etc. - Such were their names, and both of them were in the chamber of the [Temple] courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:5:3.hebrew: בגלגל - טור"ן בלע"ז. אבל במדינה — לא. טעמא מפרש בגמרא: משום שמא ימלא לגינתו ולחורבתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:5:3.english: With a wheel - Torn in Old French [a windlass]. But in the rest of the country, [it is] not [permitted]. The reason is explained in the Gemara: because [of a decree] lest one draw [water] for his garden or for his ruin.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:5:4.hebrew: ומבאר הקר בי"ט - ולא בשבת. ובגמרא מפרש מאי ניהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:5:4.english: And from the Heker Well on a Festival - But not on Shabbat. And in the Gemara, it explains what it is.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:6:1.english: From Pashronya - [The name of] a place.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:6:2.english: And scatters [it] in it - Spreads [it] out in it.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:7:1.hebrew: דלא מבטל ליה - וליכא משום אשוויי גומות, דמלאכה הוא בשבת, דהוי כבנין; דמידי דחזי למאכל בהמה או לטיט החומות לא מבטיל ליה התם. אבל מלח, משנדרס ברגל לא חזי, ומסתמא מבטיל ליה, ובמדינה אסור:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:7:1.english: As one does not negate it - And there is no [issue] on account of leveling depressions, which is a [prohibited] labor on Shabbat, as it is akin to building; for an item that is suitable for animal feed or for wall mortar, one does not negate it there. But salt, once it has been trampled underfoot, is not fit [for anything], and presumably one negates it, and [therefore] outside the Temple it is forbidden.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:8:1.hebrew: קא מוסיף אבנין - ואפילו בחול אסור להוסיף על המזבח, דכתיב: "הכל בכתב מיד ה' עלי השכיל", שהבנין נמסר לדוד על ידי הנביאים, שלא להוסיף ושלא לגרוע. ואית דנקטי ליה משום שבת, ולא היא; דהא בכסוי הדם בשחיטת חולין (חולין פג:), דאיירי בחול, הכי נמי פרכינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:8:1.english: He adds to the structure - And even on a weekday it is forbidden to add to the Altar, as it is written: “All this in writing from the hand of the Lord, He made me understand” (I Chronicles 28:19), for the [plan of the] building was transmitted to David through the prophets, neither to add nor to subtract. And there are those who take it [to be forbidden] because of Shabbat, but that is not so; for regarding the covering of the blood in [tractate] Shechitat Chullin (Chullin 83b), which deals with a weekday, we also raise this objection.

Rashi on Eruvin 104a:9:1.hebrew: הא קא הוי חציצה - בין רגליהם לכבש. וחציצה כי האי גוונא פסולה, דתנן בשחיטת קדשים (זבחים טו:): "כל הזבחים שקבל דמן זר, ואונן, וערל, יושב, ועומד על גבי כלי, על גבי רגל בהמה, וע"ג רגל חבירו — פסול". והתם יליף טעמא:
Rashi on Eruvin 104a:9:1.english: Behold, it constitutes an interposition - Between their feet and the ramp. And an interposition of this kind invalidates [the service], as we learned in a mishna in Shechitat Kodashim (Zevachim 15b): "All sacrifices whose blood was collected by a non-priest, an onan, an uncircumcised [priest], [one who was] sitting, or [one who was] standing on a vessel, on the foot of an animal, or on the foot of his fellow — [are] invalid." And there [the Gemara] derives the reason.

Tosafot on Eruvin 104a:12:1.hebrew: דרש רבא חצר שנתקלקלה - הלכתא כדמסיק, דלא ירדה לא בסל ולא בקופה, אלא בשולי קופה שנשתברה ונשארו בה השוליים, כדפירש בקונטרס. אי נמי: הופך הקופה ונותנה על שוליה, דהיינו על ידי שינוי. אבל ביד — נראה לר"י דאסור:
Tosafot on Eruvin 104a:12:1.english: Rava taught: A courtyard that was damaged - The halakhah is in accordance with what [the Gemara] concludes, that one should not go down [into the courtyard] either with a basket or with a tub, but rather with the bottom of a basket that broke and its bottom remained, as [Rashi] explained in the commentary. Alternatively, he turns the tub over and places [the straw] on its bottom, that is to say, by means of an alteration. But [bringing it] by hand appears to the Ri to be forbidden.

Tosafot on Eruvin 104a:20:1.hebrew: הכי גריס בקונטרס אלא הא דאמר רב נשים המשחקות באגוזים כו' לא משום אשוויי גומות דאי לא תימא הכי כו' - ותימה: תרתי דרב למה לי? ומיהו י"ל, דחדא מכלל חברתה איתמר. ור"ח גרס הכי: "אלא דאמר רב יהודה: נשים המשחקות באגוזים כו', לא, דמשתמע קלא כי זמזומי" — פירוש: שזורק אחד ומקבל אחד בהשמעת קול, דאסור. והדר קאמר: "ואלא הא דאמר רב יהודה: נשים המשחקות בתפוחים כו'", ומשני: "לא, משום אשוויי גומות". והשתא תרי ענייני איסור אשמעינן. ומיהו, אין למחות בנשים ותינוקות, דמוטב שיהו שוגגין ואל יהו מזידין. פר"ח דהלכתא כעולא, דאפילו קול שאינו של שיר אסור; אף על גב דשני רבה כל הני תיובתא דאקשי ליה, אשנויי לא סמכינן. ורב אלפס והר"ר יהודה בר ברזיליי פסקו כרבה, דרב אחא בר יעקב מתרץ אליביה, וקאי אמימר נמי כוותיה, דשרא למימלא בגילגולא במחוזא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 104a:20:1.english: This is the reading in the Kuntres: "Rather, that which Rav said: Women who play with nuts etc. — No, [it is] because of leveling depressions, for if you do not say so etc." - And it is astonishing: Why do I need two [rulings] of Rav? However, it can be said that one was stated by inference from the other. And Rabbeinu Chananel read as follows: "Rather, that which Rav Yehuda said: Women who play with nuts etc. — No, for its sound sounds like humming" — the explanation being that one tosses one [nut] and catches another with the production of sound, which is prohibited. And then [the Gemara] says: "And rather, that which Rav Yehuda said: Women who play with apples etc.," and it answers: "No, [it is] because of leveling depressions." And now, [the Gemara] teaches us two distinct prohibitions. However, one should not protest against women and children, for it is better that they be unwitting [transgressors] and not be willful [transgressors]. Rabbeinu Chananel explained that the halakha is according to Ulla, that even a sound that is not musical is prohibited; although Rabba resolved all of these objections that were raised against him, we do not rely on [such] resolutions. And Rav Alfas and Rabbi Yehuda ben Barzillai ruled according to Rabba, since Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov resolves [the sources] according to his view, and Ameimar also stands in agreement with him, for he permitted drawing [water] with a wheel in Meḥoza.

Tosafot on Eruvin 104a:24:1.hebrew: גזרה שמא ימלא לגינתו ולחורבתו - מפרש רבינו תם, דדוקא בגלגלים גדולים, שממלאין הרבה מים ביחד, שייך למיגזר; אבל שלנו — קטנים הם, ולא גזרינן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 104a:24:1.english: A decree lest he draw [water] for his garden and for his ruin - Rabbeinu Tam explains that specifically regarding large wheels, which draw up a lot of water at once, is it relevant to issue a decree; but ours are small, and we do not decree [against them].

Tosafot on Eruvin 104a:3:1.hebrew: לישמעינן צלצול קטן - אי צלצול אסור במדינה, פריך שפיר: לישמעינן צלצול, דבמקדש מותר ובמדינה אסור. אבל נראה לר"י דצלצול שרי במדינה, וקשיא: דאם כן, מאי פריך? ומפרש ר"י דפריך הכי: דליתני במתניתין, "כהן שלקה באצבע כורך לו צלצול — בין במקדש בין במדינה; ואם להוציא דם — כאן וכאן אסור":
Tosafot on Eruvin 104a:3:1.english: Let [the mishna] teach us [the case of] a small sash - If a sash is forbidden in the country, [the Gemara] asks well: Let [the mishna] teach us [the case of] a sash, which is permitted in the Temple and forbidden in the country. But it appears to the Ri that a sash is permitted in the country, and it is difficult: for if so, what is [the Gemara] asking? And the Ri explains that it asks as follows: That [the mishna] should teach in our Mishnah: "A priest whose finger was injured may wrap a sash around it, whether in the Temple or in the country; and if [it is] to draw blood, it is forbidden both here and there."
